messages.text: Sunday edition · Canton, Michigan
A clear afternoon, a listening-room night, and the week on deck
Clear and breezy right now, with light-drizzle odds later. The best near-term move is a low-key local outing; tonight, The Ark has the sharpest ticketed pick.
Canton is clear at 74.5°F with a west wind; the forecast tops out near 75°F, with a 22% chance of drizzle.
Late-August light lingers until 8:22 PM. The waxing gibbous moon is 78% illuminated and rises at 6:10 PM.
Choose your Sunday speed

The easy daytime answer is Cruisin' Hines: free for spectators, about 12 miles away, and running until 4 PM. Tonight, Tray Wellington at The Ark brings adventurous banjo and bluegrass to Ann Arbor at 7:30.
A family birthday arrives Wednesday—three days away.
Michigan's big signals: trade, budgets, and local power

Canada's planned tariff response puts cross-border manufacturing and agriculture in focus. Elsewhere, Michigan revenue is running ahead of forecasts, while a court affirmed Washtenaw County's control of its own local resources.
The week gets interesting quickly
Book or browse now: JDs Stage Bistro opens Tuesday in Chelsea, Rush plays Detroit Wednesday and Friday, and Canton's $10 Emu-sical opens Friday.
Space is having a quietly excellent week
NASA's Starling mission navigated without GPS, Roman cleared flight readiness ahead of its August 30 target, and Hubble traced a formative Milky Way collision.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September. Ship 41 completed static-fire testing, but SpaceX has not posted an official date.
Breezy daylight, a rising moon, and one good plan is plenty.
Monday, August 24 · Canton, Michigan
Cool start, clear runway, and a small plan worth making
A clear late-summer Monday gives way to a week of local decisions and strong small-room outings. Tonight's no-fuss option costs less than a cup of coffee.
Canton starts clear at 52.3°F; the day reaches about 76°F with only a 1% chance of precipitation.
The waxing gibbous moon is 85.4% illuminated and rises at 6:47 PM, with sunset arriving at 8:20 PM.
A quiet Monday with one easy nightcap
The easy answer tonight is Blind Pig Comedy in Ann Arbor: doors at 8 PM, a $2.50 ticket, and a 21+ room. Keep it casual and buy before you head out.
A family birthday lands midweek—two days away.
Local choices, regional stakes

Plymouth Township is poised to consider its first master-plan update in 11 years, while Canton has set a free September hazardous-waste roundup. At the regional scale, Canada’s planned tariff response remains a major Michigan economic story.
Tuesday has excellent branching paths
Tuesday offers a free saahnjoo happy hour in Ann Arbor, JDs Stage Bistro’s opening night in Chelsea, and Rush in Detroit. Pick your price point, then move early.
Orbit, autonomy, and ancient galaxies
NASA’s Starling satellites navigated without GPS, Roman is cleared for final launch preparations ahead of its August 30 target, and Hubble found new evidence of the Milky Way’s early assembly.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
A crisp start, a clear sky, and room to choose your own tempo.
Wednesday, August 26 · Canton, Michigan
Clear at dawn, local momentum by day, big sky by night
A clear morning gives way to a chance of drizzle, while Canton has fresh reasons to look ahead—from a remodeled grocer to a free fall arts festival. Overhead, Roman is edging toward launch.
Canton starts clear at 58.8°F. The day reaches about 81°F, with a 44% chance of light drizzle.
The waxing gibbous moon is 96.2% illuminated and rises at 7:43 PM, just before the 8:17 PM sunset.
A family birthday arrives today.
Canton looks ahead

Busch’s Canton remodel has added more than 1,600 products, with a public ribbon cutting set for September 4. The township’s free ARToberfest follows September 26, while a Michigan voter-ID ballot proposal faces a court challenge after missing certification.
Autonomy, astronomy, and a telescope on deck
NASA’s Starling satellites navigated without GPS, Roman is in final launch preparations for an August 30 target, and Hubble has sharpened the story of the Milky Way’s early growth.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Keep an eye on the clouds, then make something of the evening.
Thursday, August 27 · Canton, Michigan
A mostly clear Thursday, a Canton gallery opening, and a nearly full moon
The weather turns mostly clear, Canton gets an evening photography reception, and NASA is busy both testing Moon-landing exhaust and expanding its deep-space listening network.
Mostly clear skies, a high near 82°F, and only a 3% chance of precipitation: a clean late-August reset.
The moon is 99.1% illuminated and rises at 8:05 PM, just before the 8:16 PM sunset.
Canton’s creative season is coming into focus
The Ann Arbor Camera Club opens a free Canton reception tonight from 6–8 PM. Looking ahead, Plymouth’s Fall Festival runs September 11–13, followed by Canton’s free ARToberfest on September 26.
The space program is practicing for the real messes

NASA is firing simulated lander plumes into lunar soil to study the debris problem, while a new Goldstone antenna has begun handling deep-space missions. Roman remains in final preparations for its August 30 target.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Save a little evening for the moon—or a wall of good photographs.
Friday, August 28 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies, a full moon, and useful local signals

A mild, overcast Friday has a full moon waiting just after sunset. Close to home, a lower-interest tax-payment plan has reopened while Plymouth Township’s growth and fire-service strain are both in view.
Overcast with a high near 82°F, a low around 59°F, and only a 2% chance of precipitation.
Tonight’s full moon rises at 8:26 PM, 12 minutes after the 8:14 PM sunset.
Practical help—and pressure points—close to home

Wayne County’s reopened payment plan lets qualifying Plymouth and Canton owner-occupants consolidate delinquent property taxes at 6% interest. Plymouth Township also reported a July high in permits alongside increased fire calls and temporary Station 2 closures.
Weather satellites and deep-space hardware, on the clock

ESA has launched a new high-frequency weather imager for Europe and northern Africa, while NASA’s newest Goldstone antenna is already handling deep-space missions. Roman remains in final preparations for its August 30 target.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Let the clouds keep it soft; the moon will do the lighting later.
Saturday, August 29 · Canton, Michigan
Warm, cloudy, and looking past the weekend
An overcast day near 84°F makes room for an easy weekend pace. Locally, Plymouth Township is teeing up a November parks vote, while NASA’s Swift observatory is back to catching cosmic surprises.
Overcast with a high near 84°F, a low around 54°F, and only a 1% chance of precipitation.
The moon remains 98.8% illuminated and rises at 8:46 PM, after the 8:12 PM sunset.
Parks, property taxes, and a practical fall agenda

Plymouth Township voters will decide in November whether to renew the existing parks levy through 2030. For qualifying Plymouth and Canton homeowners, Wayne County’s reopened payment plan cuts interest on consolidated past-due property taxes to 6%.
A veteran observatory gets back in the game

NASA’s 21-year-old Swift observatory has resumed X-ray and ultraviolet observations, though its Burst Alert Telescope remains offline. Europe’s new high-frequency weather imager is headed toward faster severe-storm views, while Roman targets August 30.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Cloudy overhead, cosmic surprises elsewhere—either way, look up.
Sunday, August 30 · Canton, Michigan
A soft-weather Sunday, roadwork ahead, and Roman’s moment
Light-drizzle odds shape a warm Sunday, and Ann Arbor’s North University–Thayer project continues into the coming week. In space, Roman has a launch target today.
A warm day near 83°F with a 25% chance of light drizzle; the evening stays mild around 67°F.
The waning gibbous moon is 95.4% illuminated and rises at 9:07 PM, well after the 8:11 PM sunset.
A practical week starts taking shape

North University remains closed to through traffic between State and Fletcher as Ann Arbor continues streetscape and utility work next week. Qualifying Plymouth and Canton owner-occupants can use Wayne County’s reopened 6% interest payment plan for past-due property taxes.
A launch target, a veteran telescope, and a very busy sky

NASA’s Roman telescope targets no earlier than 7:26 a.m. EDT today. Swift has resumed X-ray and ultraviolet observations, while Europe’s new weather imager aims to sharpen severe-storm views after commissioning.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Let the drizzle be a nudge toward a slower Sunday.
Monday, August 31 · Canton, Michigan
A humid Monday, roots music at night, and a telescope in deep space
Warm, drizzly late-summer weather sets the tone, but evening offers both brewery opera and roots music. Farther out, Roman is now on its way toward the Sun–Earth L2 point.
Overcast and humid with a high near 87°F, a low around 67°F, and a 21% chance of light drizzle.
The waning gibbous moon is 89.9% illuminated and rises at 9:31 PM, well after the 8:09 PM sunset.
A Monday evening with unexpectedly good choices

The easy answer is Opera by the Glass at 734 Brewing: free, close-up, and delightfully un-boring—just reserve a spot. For a larger small-room night, The Brudi Brothers bring rootsy Americana to The Ark at 8 PM.
A personal upkeep task is scheduled tomorrow morning.
A few local details worth routing around

Textile Road is closed between Tuttle Hill Road and Huron River Drive for DTE work, with a roughly two-week timeline. North University remains closed to through traffic in Ann Arbor, while Plymouth District Library is gathering input for upcoming technology classes.
Tomorrow has tacos, trivia, and a simple lunch escape

Tomorrow, make a team for free Tacos & Trivia at Campus Martius or take a food-truck lunch break at Cadillac Square. The Michigan State Fair opens September 3 in Novi if you want a Labor Day-weekend anchor.
Roman has left the pad; deep space is calling

NASA’s Roman telescope has launched and separated from its Falcon Heavy, beginning a roughly three-month trip to Sun–Earth L2. Swift is back to X-ray and ultraviolet observations, and NASA’s newest Goldstone antenna is adding deep-space capacity.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
A little rain, a little opera, and a telescope heading out of town.
Tuesday, September 1 · Canton, Michigan
A steamy September start, games tonight, and robots below the waves

September begins hot and overcast, with an easy game-night option in Ann Arbor. Nearby, Plymouth-Canton schools are lowering activity fees; far offshore, NOAA robots are extending the seafloor survey.
Overcast and hot, with a high near 95°F, a low around 69°F, and a 10% chance of precipitation.
The waning gibbous moon is 82.3% illuminated and rises at 9:59 PM, long after the 8:07 PM sunset.
Pick your kind of low-pressure social night

The easy answer is Sylvan Factory’s free Game Night from 5–10 PM: board games, mini painting, and beginner-friendly RPG one-shots. For a more old-school spin, English country dancing starts at 7 PM with live music and no partner needed.
Labor Day is six days away.
A little more room to join in

Plymouth-Canton schools have approved $500,000 for athletics and activities, reducing participation fees and adding support for clubs and performance groups. Plymouth District Library is also collecting input to shape fall technology classes.
Tomorrow’s small rooms are doing their thing
Tomorrow, catch Jeremy Siegrist’s free early set at North Star, take the microphone at The Ark’s $3 Open Stage, or settle into the North Star poetry open mic.
Robots are mapping the places ships can’t reach

NOAA’s long-range underwater robots have gathered more than 68,000 images along over 200 nautical miles of seafloor for the Atlantic sea-scallop assessment. Roman continues toward Sun–Earth L2, while Swift is back to X-ray and ultraviolet work.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Heat outside, board games inside, robots far below—September has range.
Wednesday, September 2 · Canton, Michigan
A hot Wednesday, old-school print, and a fiery satellite farewell
Overcast heat is the day’s background noise. Tonight invites hands-on play in Ann Arbor, while a Canton student radio station opens fall applications and ESA studies a satellite’s final flight.
Overcast and hot, with a high near 96°F, a low around 72°F, and a 25% chance of precipitation.
The waning gibbous moon is 73% illuminated and rises at 10:33 PM, after the 8:06 PM sunset.
A hands-on Wednesday with room to improvise

The easy answer is A2 Crokinole Club at Lowertown: free, welcoming, and satisfyingly flickable from 6–8 PM. For something tactile in a different century, try AADL’s free Letterpress Open Lab from 5–7 PM.
Labor Day is five days away.
Local systems are moving—on roads and on airwaves

U-M says campus construction is slowing Ann Arbor traffic and buses, with 10–15 extra minutes advised at peak times. In Plymouth-Canton, 88.1 The Park is accepting fall applications for student radio roles through September 25.
Tomorrow, choose blues, a mic, or the fair
Tomorrow brings free Deacon Earl blues and a free Queer Open Mic at North Star. The Michigan State Fair also opens in Novi for a Labor Day-weekend-sized outing.
Currents, robots, and a meticulously measured goodbye

NOAA has documented a rapid post-2014 strengthening of the Gulf Stream downstream of Florida, while its underwater robots keep surveying seafloor beyond a ship’s reach. ESA recorded a targeted satellite reentry to the second, yielding rare breakup data.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
Stay cool, make something with your hands, and leave room for a little wonder.
Thursday, September 3 · Canton, Michigan
Rainy heat, live words, and a new shape around Saturn
Light rain arrives with late-summer heat, while a strong Thursday menu runs from euchre to a rare local reading. Hubble has spotted an evolving 10-sided wave around Saturn’s south pole.
Light rain, a high near 96°F, and a 28% chance of precipitation: hot weather with a little texture.
The last-quarter moon is 62.4% illuminated and rises at 11:17 PM, well after the 8:04 PM sunset.
Three good ways to leave the house

The easy answer is free drop-in euchre at AADL Westgate from 5:30–7:30 PM. If you want a bigger outing, the Michigan State Fair opens in Novi today; for a free musical detour, catch Deacon Earl at North Star.
Labor Day is four days away.
September’s local calendar is getting crowded

Plymouth Township will hear a proposed Haggerty Road multi-sport complex on September 16. Ann Arbor has added a new football-game-day street closure for Sept. 5, while 88.1 The Park is recruiting student staff.
Tomorrow: jazz, comedy, or headphones
Tomorrow, start the free Detroit Jazz Festival or take a free headphone dance break at AADL. Tam White’s stand-up offers a ticketed Ann Arbor nightcap.
Saturn gets stranger; radio science gets more useful

Hubble has found an evolving decagon in Saturn’s south-polar jet stream. NASA’s multi-sensor rocket revealed unexpected structure in radio-disrupting ionospheric clouds, while ESA’s Samba reentry is yielding rare debris-breakup data.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; neither SpaceX nor current launch tracking supports a more precise time.
A little rain, a little euchre, and one very strange planet.
Friday, September 4 · Canton, Michigan
Rainy Friday, free jazz, and Mercury on the horizon
Rain showers arrive as the Detroit Jazz Festival opens. Plymouth manufacturing has fresh momentum, while BepiColombo has shed its transfer stage on the way to Mercury.
Rain showers, a high near 81°F, and a 67% chance of precipitation: keep the umbrella close.
The last-quarter moon is 51.1% illuminated and rises just after midnight.
Let the rain choose the soundtrack
The easy answer is the free Detroit Jazz Festival, opening at 5 PM. For an indoor, free, and oddball alternative, AADL’s Silent Disco starts at 5:30 PM.
Labor Day is three days away.
Work and traffic are both changing shape

Norm Fasteners has acquired a Plymouth automotive-bolt plant and plans to retain its workforce, while American Rheinmetall has delivered an XM30 prototype with Plymouth-made turrets. Ann Arbor’s football-day closures begin tomorrow.
Labor Day weekend has officially started
Build the weekend around free Detroit Jazz Festival stages or the Michigan State Fair in Novi.
Mercury is getting closer

BepiColombo has separated from its transfer stage and is headed toward November Mercury-orbit insertion. NASA’s multi-sensor rocket has also revealed unexpected structure in radio-disrupting ionospheric clouds.
Flight 14 remains no earlier than September; no precise time is supported.
Rain on the pavement, brass in the city, and Mercury ahead.
Friday, September 5 · Canton, Michigan
A softer, drizzly Friday
Heavy drizzle is the day’s invitation to keep plans loose and the pace low.
Heavy drizzle with a high near 76°F, a low around 62°F, and an 18% chance of precipitation.
The last-quarter moon is 39.6% illuminated and rises at 1:21 AM Saturday.
A gentle-weather day for a smaller orbit.
